comment: Delegated/proxy authority should be modelled as a lifecycle, not inferred from relationships. The Client Registry models parent-child and guardian relationships, while the LHR enforces individual consent preferences. The architecture does not explicitly distinguish a relationship record from current authority to grant, modify or withdraw permissions on another person's behalf. Relationship alone should not imply permission authority.

public.text: Delegated/proxy authority should be modelled as a lifecycle, not inferred from relationships. The Client Registry models parent-child and guardian relationships, while the LHR enforces individual consent preferences. The architecture does not explicitly distinguish a relationship record from current authority to grant, modify or withdraw permissions on another person's behalf. Relationship alone should not imply permission authority.
public.suggestedRevision: Extend the consent/permissions profile to support delegated or proxy authority as a governed, time-bounded relationship. Represent the subject, representative/delegate, legal or governance basis, scope, purpose/data category, effective period, status, modification, expiry/revocation and audit provenance. Client Registry relationships may support identity resolution but should not themselves imply decision-making authority; national law should determine who is authorised and under what conditions.
